source.title: From Behavior to Mechanism: Tracing Divergent Response Modes in Frontier Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a difference-in-means residual-stream direction and activation addition/ablation to investigate a different behavior: clarification-seeking derail versus substantive answers on values-conflict items. It does not test refusal or the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: The mechanistic results concern derail/answer behavior, not refusal of harmful requests or refusal of harmless requests. They are recorded under versions ["none"] and fits_no_version, not as evidence for the claim versions. The paper cites the original refusal-direction work, but does not report results from that work as its own.
record.test_reason: The study borrows the refusal-direction method (difference-in-means direction, activation addition, all-layer projection ablation per Arditi et al.) and applies it to Llama-3.3-70B's clarification-seeking 'derail' behavior on mildly values-conflicting items. It does not measure refusal of harmful or harmless requests, and derail is defined as neither complying nor refusing. Its mechanistic results therefore bear on no claim version and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that Llama's derail-versus-answer split is decodable before generation and controlled by a difference-in-means direction. Adding it raises derails to 86%; ablating it cuts the rate from 42% to 18% and from 46% to 10%. They say the direction carries most, not all, of the behavior. The paper's main conclusions are behavioral differences across six frontier models.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a difference-in-means residual direction, activation addition, and projection ablation, but the direction distinguishes derail from substantive-answer items rather than harmful from harmless instructions or refusal. Its intervention is at layer 40 for addition and projects the same direction out at all 80 layers.
record.method_sensitivity: The direction is measured at the generation-onset position; the intervention is applied at layer 40 for addition and at all 80 layers for ablation. The paper reports distinct effects across steering strengths and complementary train/test splits.

fits_no_version.finding: A linear probe on generation-onset residual activations decodes derail versus other responses at 0.83–0.87 balanced accuracy (layers 36–76), against 0.72 for a Llama-3.2-1B prompt-only control.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A pre-generation residual representation in Llama-3.3-70B predicts clarification-seeking derail on values-conflict items.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding the derail-minus-other difference-in-means direction at layer 40 moves the derail rate monotonically from 0% (α=−12) to 86% (α=+12), against 40% at α=0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A difference-in-means direction causally controls derail behavior in Llama-3.3-70B, as a non-refusal analogue of the refusal-direction method.

fits_no_version.finding: All-layer projection ablation of the fitted direction cuts derails from 21 to 9 and from 23 to 5 of 50 in the two splits. Equal-norm random ablation changes nothing. Some derails survive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The derail direction carries most but not all of the derail behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Directions fitted on complementary halves have cosine 0.82 (random control 0.01).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The derail direction is reproducible across data halves.

record.problems: The mechanistic analysis uses 100 base items split into halves, with 50 test items per intervention split. The authors note that mechanistic computations use reference weights that are not byte-identical to Together's hosted serving stack, though they report close agreement on the behavior. Probe labels come from the study's model-judge consensus; the authors also acknowledge that part of the larger model's probe advantage over the 1B control may reflect its reading prompt ambiguity in more detail. These limitations concern the study's derail behavior, not the refusal claim.

untested.parts: All: no harmful-minus-harmless direction, and no refusal rate under ablation or addition. Capability preservation is reported only qualitatively ('fluent and on-task'), for the derail direction.
All: no weight edit or abliteration.
All: no jailbreaks and no adversarial training.
All: no multi-direction or cone analysis of refusal.
All: no cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer of a refusal direction. The 1B probe is a prompt-ambiguity control, not a transfer test.
All: DeepSeek-R1 traces are analyzed behaviorally only, with no direction analysis in reasoning models.

record.verdict_notes: The derail label explicitly excludes refusal ('does not clearly comply, refuse, or offer alternative'), so no row measures refusal. The paper also reports behavioral refusal-with-alternative and refusal-override rates, but with no direction analysis, so these do not bear on any version. A ridge-direction comparison (AUC and stability) is a comparison of methods and correctly has no row. One could argue for T6, since only the method, not the finding, is reused; T4 is kept because the paper relies on Arditi et al.'s ablation procedure as its tool.

versions.untested_parts: Refusal on harmful and harmless requests; preservation of general abilities during refusal-direction ablation.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration test.
No jailbreak suppression of a refusal direction and no training against its ablation.
No test of whether refusal is represented by an affine structure, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No transfer test across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models for a refusal direction.
No test of how refusal training determines whether a removable refusal direction exists.
No test of the refusal-direction claim in reasoning models.

relation.reason: The refusal-direction technique is used as a tool on a non-refusal behavior (clarification-seeking derail versus other labels on mild values-conflict items), and the refusal claim itself is not tested.

tranche.reason: The study borrows the difference-in-means, activation-addition and all-layer projection-ablation method (citing Arditi et al.) for a 'derail' behavior. The appendix rubric defines derail as not clearly complying or refusing. It never measures refusal, so its results do not bear on any version.

source_check.notes: The derail direction is explicitly not a refusal direction; the rubric defines derail as not clearly complying or refusing. Rows fit no version. The text pairs rates with alpha only at 0 and the two extremes; the other pairings are inferred. No capability benchmark is reported, only 'fluent and on-task'. Minor inconsistency: the alpha=0 control is 40% (20/50), while the first-split no-hook arm is 21/50. The authors_conclusion paraphrase is correct.
